author: minimalmonk
text: Hi MitchWorse, im doing QM homework now and i still dont get it enough. its acceptable qm formation on your chart? its looks for me more like double bottom at all. you have L,H,LL,HH - fully agreed but the "trigger arm" is noticeably lower than first low. its ok for that formation? if yes, i could find a lot more formations so far. maybe be purist is not necessary... btw. what means "LQ"? /thanks

author: MitchWorse
text:
Hey!

As long as the "trigger" doesn't make another LL i'm anticipating a reversal. The most important is the HH(buyers made a statement: "We're here, come and get us!"). If sellers then can't push it below the LL, the odds are with the buyers.(consuming supply i.e. clearing the way up)

Some place pending orders at the L-price with a stop just below LL.

Another thing to keep in mind is that the QM is a reversal pattern. It has to follow a strong move imho.

LQ = LiQuidity after CP into a nearby S/D(exhaustion spike) (all these terms:P)
